seoTitle: Free Randomised Crontab Generator to Spread Jobs
metaDescription: Spread many cron jobs across minutes and hours instead of firing all at :00, with stable per-job hashes. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Enter your jobs and get crontab lines that spread them across minutes or hours instead of all firing at the same time. Times are stable per job, like Jenkins H syntax, or evenly spaced.
why:
When every job is set to run at minute zero, the machine sees a spike at the top of each hour: backups, reports, API polling and cleanups all start together. Shared servers, rate-limited APIs and remote services feel it too. Choosing odd minutes by hand helps for a while, until someone copies a line and the spike returns.

This generator assigns minutes from a hash of a seed and the command, so a given job always lands at the same time, but different jobs differ. Or it spaces them evenly across a window. Pick the frequency, the allowed hours and an optional user. Nothing is uploaded, and the same seed gives the same schedule when you regenerate it.
howTo: List your jobs, one command per line.
Choose how often they should run and the hour window, if any.
Select stable hashing or even spacing, and enter a seed and optional user.
Copy the crontab lines into your crontab file.

faq.a: A hash of the seed and the command picks the minute, so regenerating the list gives the same times. Add or remove a job and the others do not move, which keeps change history clean.
When you want a predictable gap between jobs, for example to stay below a rate limit. Hashing gives a random-looking spread, while even spacing distributes jobs at fixed intervals across the window.

faq.q: Does it change the time zone?
faq.a: No. Cron lines are interpreted in the server's time zone or the one your scheduler is set to. Use the cron time zone converter if you need to shift a schedule between zones.
